own.bio: Strange but true stories, told quietly. New odd hour, every week.

posts.caption: In 2021, one engineer typed one wrong command and 3.5 billion people lost the internet in a single instant. Not hacked. Not attacked. Just one wrong line of code during a routine maintenance check. Facebook's own engineers couldn't even log in to fix it, their access tools were on the same servers that just vanished. They had to physically drive to data centers and override servers by hand. One by one. 6 hours. $60 million lost every single hour. And the exact same vulnerability? Still exists right now. The internet is more fragile than you think.

2021 mein ek engineer ne ek galat command type ki aur 3.5 billion logon ka internet ek pal mein band ho gaya. Hack nahi hua. Attack nahi hua. Bas ek routine maintenance check ke dauran ek galat line of code. 6 ghante. Har ghante 60 million dollar ka nuksaan. Internet utna strong nahi jitna hum sochte hain.

There is a sound that only 2% of people can hear. Scientists have studied it for 50 years and still have no answer. It's called The Hum — and the leading theory is that it's the Earth itself vibrating at a frequency most humans aren't built to detect. A woman heard it for 11 years, moved across the country to escape it, and it followed her to the new house. Stop right now, close your eyes, and listen. What do you hear?

We call space the final frontier. But we've barely explored our own planet. Earth is stranger than anything we've found out there — and most people have no idea. From perfect solar eclipses to oceans deeper than mountains are tall, this is the planet you thought you knew.

In 1974, a man calculated the exact day he would die and spent a year preparing for it. What happened next is stranger than the prediction itself. Frank was obsessed with numerology. He told his family, quit his job, and gave away everything he owned. When the day came and went without incident, he thought he'd beaten fate. He hadn't.

recentPosts.caption: What if continents and oceans switched places? The Pacific becomes a supercontinent. Earth's deepest point is Everest Deep, and is almost nine kilometers below sea-level. And the Mid-Atlantic Canyon divides the world from pole to pole. Life finds a way but struggles in this new, upside-down world. This all sounds cool, until the oxygen runs out.

Pigeons are basically GPS Drones with superpowers. They can pinpoint their own location hundreds of kilometers from their roosts and navigate home autonomously, only using smell, the Sun, and even Earth’s magnetic field.

No one works harder than our rover driver Yolk, who is tirelessly collecting nuggets every day so that the space station can function smoothly.

Have you already started your space adventure? Star Birds, which we developed together with our friends at @toukana_interactive, is available on Steam!
Two billion years ago, the world’s first nuclear reactors appeared in Oklo, Gabon. They were NOT made by humans and were self-regulating and accident-free.

In the late 9th century, Vikings have raided kingdom after kingdom and nearly conquered all of England. Wealthy monasteries and defenseless nuns were especially tempting targets and often suffered great losses. However, all of that stopped when Vikings were confronted by princess Aethelflaed, daughter of Alfred the Great.

Who was Lady of Mercia, and how did she shape the history of England by becoming Vikings' greatest nightmare? Watch our latest Nightshift video to find out! 🌚
Laughing gas can make you feel relaxed and euphoric in seconds. But it comes with serious risks as well. So, what exactly is laughing gas and why does it feel so good?

In the 17th century in Germany, one of Europe’s most terrifying witch hunts turned the town of Bamberg against itself. Tortures that occurred in the "Witch Factory" forced innocent people to name friends, neighbors and family members, creating a deadly chain reaction that eventually reached even the richest and most powerful, while those running the trials profited from the people they condemned.

How did a witch hunt grow so powerful that almost nobody was safe? And what finally brought one of
What if you could skip the boring and painful parts of life? It sounds tempting until you realize what you’d lose along the way. Time doesn’t really stop, and neither does the world.
Brace yourself... 😔

We’re working on 12 monthly challenges for our factory-building game Star Birds. And we want to name each challenge after a star constellation!

We’re not looking for the usual suspects like Capricorn, Gemini or Scorpio. We want weird, creative, charming, ridiculous or completely made-up constellations instead.

Got an idea? Drop your constellation names in the comments! Our favorite suggestions might actually make it into the game.

recentPosts.caption:
This dome getaway looks like it belongs on another planet. ⁠
⁠
Located in the Joshua Tree desert, Sandora Domes is a one-of-a-kind stay where you can sleep beneath the stars, relax by the pool, and unwind in the spa surrounded by the high desert.⁠
⁠
With its curved domes, open-air spaces, and quiet desert setting, it feels more like a private escape than a typical getaway.⁠
⁠
By: @sandoradomes @kuratekphoto @cure.realestate⁠
Managed by: @stayfieldtrip

A once-in-a-lifetime experience with a purpose. 🦏🌿⁠
A glimpse into the work of @careforwild where volunteers help care for injured and orphaned rhinos with the ultimate goal of returning them to the wild. ⁠
⁠
From rehabilitation to rewilding, every step brings these incredible animals closer to a life where they belong, healthy, protected, and free.⁠
🎥: @fenivanova

This Japanese artist turns fallen leaves into tiny works of art. 🍃⁠
⁠
Tokyo-based artist Lito uses fallen leaves as his canvas, carefully cutting away tiny pieces to create detailed scenes featuring animals, nature, and Japanese art.⁠
⁠
He started creating leaf art in 2020 and can spend up to eight hours on a single piece, working with a small knife to bring each scene to life.⁠
⁠⁠
By: @lito_leafart

A dreamy Airbnb you’ll want to wake up in. 🌴✨⁠
Showed us this hidden oasis in Mexico, where the pool flows around the entire space, creating the feeling of having your own private tropical paradise.⁠
⁠
Would you stay here?⁠
🎥: @adiavital0

Most people assume this is years of saving away. It isn’t. Hotels have empty rooms every single night and they need content constantly, so hosting someone who can actually film the place costs them nothing but a room that was sitting empty anyway.

Born with dwarfism, Francis never grew much beyond his kitten days. He was rescued as a tiny kitten and went on to live 14 happy years with his family.⁠
⁠
He was playful, curious, and full of personality, becoming a beloved little cat to everyone who came across his story.⁠ ❤️⁠

By: @francisandmaggie

@mbassrana showed us a fresh catch with a seriously unique look. 🐟👀⁠

This might be one of Spain’s most mystical forests. ⁠
⁠
Gorbeia Natural Park is filled with ancient beech trees, moss-covered paths, and misty woodland that feels straight out of a fairytale.⁠
⁠
The park is home to some of the most beautiful forest scenery in northern Spain, with hiking trails winding through its quiet landscapes.⁠
⁠
By: @jabisanz

Ever seen a lake that looks like a giant bowl of matcha? 🍵🌿⁠
Qingshan Lake in China gets its unofficial nickname, “Matcha Lake,” from the bright green surface created by duckweed and microalgae, especially during the warmer months.⁠
⁠
But the real magic happens above the water. Thousands of metasequoia trees grow directly from the lake, creating an unusual aquatic forest where the trunks appear to disappear into the water as you move through it. 🌳💚⁠
🎥: @ai_gromova

Photographer @varunsikkaphotos captured the beautiful jewelry tradition of Spiti Valley. ⁠
⁠
Jewelry is an important part of traditional dress in Spiti, worn by both men and women. ⁠
⁠
Silver is the preferred metal for many traditional ornaments, often decorated with turquoise, coral, amber, and tiny seed pearls. Women may wear necklaces, earrings, bracelets, and silver amulets as part of their everyday dress, while weddings call for much more elaborate pieces.⁠
⁠

This medieval fair in Portugal takes the theme seriously… even when it comes to dessert. 🏰🥞⁠
A crepe experience that looks like it came straight out of the Middle Ages, making the perfect treat to enjoy while exploring the historic atmosphere of the fair.⁠
⁠
A feast for the eyes and, hopefully, the taste buds too. 😋⁠
🎥: @zahra_sheen_

Premium Economy just got a lot more private. ✈️⁠
⁠
Emirates has unveiled a new Premium Economy seat with a full-height privacy screen that passengers can raise or lower at the touch of a button.⁠
⁠
The new seats also come with wireless charging, USB-C ports, a phone holder and a 13.3-inch 4K screen.⁠
⁠
By: @emirates

Presented by @Rolex. Welcome to Africa 🌍 Africa Earth’s Wild Home takes you deep into the heart of our wildest continent, bringing you closer to its animals, landscapes, and the people watching over it than ever before.

Through its partnership with the National Geographic Society and as part of its Perpetual Planet Initiative, #Rolex supports expeditions exploring and protecting remarkable places around the world, a selection of which are featured in Africa Earth’s Wild Home. #PerpetualPlanet

Describe Pompeii: Out of Time in 3 words? It's Now Streaming.

#PompeiiOutOfTime with @twhiddleston is now streaming on @DisneyPlus and @hulu.

Think you need to hit 10,000 steps every day to make your walk count? New research suggests there’s another way to get more from your daily stroll: pick up the pace. Find out what scientists discovered about the relationship between step count, walking intensity, and health at the link in bio. 

Photograph by Tatiana Maksimova, Getty

Sometimes, the best view is right beneath your feet 🌿

#NationalParksUSA and #SecretsOfTheElephants are now streaming on @DisneyPlus

Summer school looks a little different for loon chicks. During their first 12 weeks, they learn essential survival skills from their parents, including how to swim, dive, and forage.

#InsideTheEnchantedWaterways is now streaming on @DisneyPlus

Fishing guide Justin Dymond spends his nights taking bowfishers out on Florida's Crystal River. But he's not the only one hunting. Bottlenose dolphins gather around his boat, using its lights to find and flush prey from hiding places—the first documented partnership of this kind in the United States. The relationship has changed how Dymond sees the cetaceans he once considered competition, and after years of watching it develop, he turned to National Geographic Explorer Stefanie Gazda to better

Photo by @jake_brass | I captured this image, “Three Beaks,” while visiting the Saltee Islands in Ireland. When these puffins began to line up, I saw the potential for a quirky image of a puffin tower and positioned myself accordingly. I was fortunate that they all posed differently, creating this unique puffin stack.

This photo was featured in our @natgeoyourshot #NatGeoYourShotOurHOME challenge.

People with POTS often also have autoimmune diseases, and similar connections are emerging in long COVID. While experts don’t classify either condition as an autoimmune disorder, evidence suggests the immune system may play a role in disrupting the nerves that regulate functions like heart rate and digestion. Researchers are now looking for the specific auto-antibodies behind this damage, which could reveal new targets for treating POTS and long COVID.

Learn more at the link in bio.

Photograph

The northern lights don’t often reach Nebraska’s skies, but strong geomagnetic storms can bring them into view a few times a year. Captured near Crawford by photographer @erikjohnsonphoto, their colorful glow illuminated the night behind an abandoned homestead. Also known as aurora borealis, the display begins when ions from the sun collide with gas atoms in Earth’s atmosphere.

See more Photos of the Day at the link in bio.

Small nocturnal animals can be difficult to track in dense rainforest canopies, leaving scientists with little information about some species. But now researchers in Panama and Peru are using thermal binoculars to follow them as they move through the trees after dark. For some, it’s the first time experts have recorded close-up, extended footage of them moving about in the wild.

Find out more at the link in bio. 

Video by Trevor and Lucy Hughes

International Space Station Commander Frank Culbertson and World Trade Center survivors Earlyne Alexander and Kelly Reyher experienced the events of 9/11 from the most disparate viewpoints imaginable. As destruction unfolded before them, people on the ground came together to help one another survive. 

Explore National Geographic’s collection of firsthand accounts, some never-before-seen, chronicling 9/11 at the link in bio.

As artists in New York watched the Twin Towers collapse in 2001, they felt an immediate need to help however they could. Within 48 hours, they had created a plan to honor the city's losses by replacing the buildings with beams of light. Twenty-five years later, the @911memorial continues to display the "Tribute in Light" installation, illuminating Manhattan each September 11. 

See how the installation is created at the link in bio.
